text:
Yara: Hey team — onboarding question dump: 1) How does 401(k) auto-enroll work? I'm eligible day 1 but confused about Roth vs Traditional and the company match schedule. 2) I start Nov 18 (mid-month) and I'm an international hire  when does medical/dental/vision actually kick in? 3) I have a home-office setup stipend (up to $500)  where/how do I submit receipts and is it taxable?

Ben: Welcome Yara! Quick answers: 1) auto-enroll defaults to 6% pre-tax (Traditional) unless you opt out or change elections in the Retirement Portal. You can switch to Roth in the portal any time; limits follow IRS annual limits. Company match: 50% match on first 6% contributions, vesting 25% per year (4-year cliff schedule).

Carlos: Add payroll timing: contributions are withheld each pay period starting with first paycheck processed after your hire paperwork clears. If you change elections they take effect after the payroll cutoff following the change.

BenefitsBot: Coverage note: For standard plans, benefits effective date for new hires is the first of the month following 30 days of employment. For special-case international hires we sometimes align carrier eligibility with local rules; please confirm country in the benefits portal.

Yara: I'm UK-based (remote hire). Does the 30-day rule still apply? And where's the Retirement Portal link?

Ben: For UK hires we use local providers; enrollment timelines can vary. In many cases UK health/benefits follow the local provider start dates (often immediate upon payroll registration)  check Benefits Portal > Country: United Kingdom for specifics. Retirement Portal link is in People Ops Quick Links (also in the onboarding checklist). I'll DM you the direct links.

Carlos: Regarding the stipend: submit receipts in Expensify -> New Expense -> Category: Home Office Stipend -> attach invoice/receipt and tag manager for approval. Stipend is treated as taxable income by payroll by default (appears on your paystub) unless it's paid via a non-taxable equipment reimbursement program. If you want non-taxable treatment, submit a request to people-ops@redwood.inference BEFORE purchase with the business justification.

Yara: If I change my 401(k) to Roth mid-year, does the company match still go to Traditional?

Ben: Good Q. Our match is contributed to a Traditional account by default (company policy) regardless of your deferral type. You can do an internal transfer after if you prefer but company contributions are posted as Traditional.

PayrollBot: Payroll cutoff reminder: next cutoff 2025-11-14 17:00 PT. Changes to 401(k) elections submitted before cutoff will apply to the next payroll. Expensify reimbursements approved before cutoff are included in next pay run.

Yara: Perfect, thanks all. DMing for links and will submit the home-office receipts tonight.

Ben: Welcome aboard! Ping if you need the vesting schedule PDF.
